targets.authors: Xie P, Kranzler HR, Poling J, Stein MB, Anton RF, Brady K, Weiss RD, Farrer L, Gelernter J
targets.title: Interactive effect of stressful life events and the serotonin transporter 5-HTTLPR genotype on posttraumatic stress disorder diagnosis in 2 independent populations
targets.evidence_quote: The purposes of this study are, first to replicate our previous finding that 5-HTTLPR genotype moderated the effect of childhood adversity on PTSD risk; and second, to test the same G×E effect again by combining the data from our previous study (1252 subjects) with those from the current study (5178 subjects) to gain greater statistical power to detect a gene-environment interaction effect.
targets.outcome_quote: The findings reported here replicate those from our previous work, adding to a growing body of research demonstrating that the 5-HTTLPR genotype moderates risk for anxiety and depression phenotypes in the context of stress and adverse events.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors give an overall replication verdict. Discussion confirms original pattern: interaction in European Americans and no detected interaction in African Americans in both studies.

reasoning: New nonoverlapping cohort explicitly retests Xie et al. 2009. Caspi and other PTSD gene studies are background, not targets; combining the old and new samples is supplementary to the independent replication.
